drivingQuestion: Did they refrain entirely, or work only privately?
outcomeNote: Dilemma raised; resolution lies beyond this unit.

segments.he: מוֹכְרֵי פֵירוֹת כְּסוּת וְכֵלִים מוֹכְרִין בְּצִנְעָה וְכוּ׳. אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: הֵן הֶחֱמִירוּ עַל עַצְמָן — דְּלָא הֲווֹ עָבְדִי כְּלָל, אוֹ דִלְמָא דַּהֲווֹ עָבְדִי בְּצִנְעָה?
segments.en: § The mishna states: On the intermediate days of a Festival, «those who sell produce, clothing, and utensils may sell» them «in private,» for the sake of the Festival. Fishermen, groats makers, and bean pounders may ply their trades in private for the sake of the Festival. Rabbi Yosei says that they were stringent with themselves. The Sages were «asked:» When it says that «they were stringent with themselves,» does it mean that «that they did not work at all» on the intermediate days of a Festival, «or perhaps» it means «that they did» their work «in private,» though it is permitted to do it publicly?

moves.about: whether 'they were stringent with themselves' means they did not work at all or worked only privately
